title: DesignPatternLanguageFile
description: Schema for one per-language realization file of a design pattern (split storage layout V8 of docs/implementation-guide.md §2.3). Joins to the main record via the main record's language_files map; the filename MUST be `pattern/<pattern>.<language>.json` where `<language>` is `generic` or one of the 13 concrete language enum values; the generic file `<name>.generic.json` carries the record's single language-neutral entry and joins as the FIRST implementation entry. Enum types are referenced from docs/pattern-schema.json (single source of truth).

pattern.description: Canonical kebab-case name of the parent DesignPattern; MUST equal the filename stem and the parent record's name

language.description: Target language of this realization; MUST equal the filename suffix. `generic` is valid only for `<name>.generic.json` (exactly one per record); concrete languages use `<name>.<language>.json`.

idiom_name.description: Name of the concrete realization (e.g. 'module-level instance', 'Meyers singleton', 'OnceCell/LazyLock', 'first-class function parameter')

implementation_notes.description: How to realize the pattern in this language; for native/idiomatic support, state explicitly what replaces the classic structure and when the classic form is still justified

code_sketch.description: Short illustrative code fragment in this language

pitfalls.description: Language-specific traps (thread-safety, ownership, listener leaks, decorator-vs-Decorator confusion, ...)

alternative.description: Preferred replacement when support is 'discouraged' (e.g. Singleton -> dependency injection); REQUIRED whenever support is 'discouraged' (this schema's conditional)

version.description: Version of THIS language realization, independent of the parent pattern's semantics (language content churns faster)

variants.description: Multiple realizations of this pattern in this language (variant-aware extension of the implicit single realization). Each variant discriminates on paradigm (pure-OO vs pure-functional vs concurrent style), a language-standard floor (min_standard, e.g. 'C++20'), and optional required language features (requires_features, e.g. 'coroutines'). The file's flat fields (idiom_name/implementation_notes/code_sketch/pitfalls/sources) MUST equal the default variant's fields - they are the joined record's summary of this language; the integrity checker enforces the equality and the uniqueness of variant_id. Schema-level uniqueness of variant_id is delegated to the checker (Draft-7 cannot extract a single key from array items).

variant_id.description: Stable slug identifying this realization within the file; referenced by default_variant

name.description: Human label of this realization (e.g. 'Boost.Asio acceptor chain (callbacks)')

min_standard.description: Language-standard/minimum-runtime floor of this variant, as the language community writes it: 'C++17', 'C++20', 'C99', 'Java 8', 'Python 3.8', 'ES2017', 'C# 8', 'Kotlin 1.9', 'Rust 2021', 'Swift 5.9' - must start with a letter and contain a digit

requires_features.description: Language features this variant needs beyond min_standard (e.g. 'coroutines', 'concepts', 'reflection')

idiom_name.description: Concrete library/idiom used by this variant (e.g. 'Boost.Asio tcp::acceptor')

implementation_notes.description: How this variant realizes the pattern; trade-offs vs the sibling variants

code_sketch.description: Short code fragment for this variant

default_variant.description: variant_id of the realization that the flat fields summarize and that GENERATE binds when no variant hint applies; REQUIRED whenever 'variants' is present (enforced by this schema's if/then), and MUST equal one of the variant_ids (checker-enforced)
